To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effect of cell-to-cell misalignment is not well described by a model that assumes the beam is displaced, and that the synchronous wave aliasing is a new phenomenon that has not been previously reported.

the synchronous wave aliasing effect in the damped DDS and the wakefield effect in the uniform structure depend on the sign of the displacement of the cell, that the synchronous wave in the damped structure is affected by the sign of the misalignment in all cases and that the synchronous wave is not affected by the beam displacement model.

1) The effect of a misalignment profile that alternates between adjacent cells with opposite signs is equivalent to a beam displacement, 2) The effect of the misalignment profile on the wakefield is the same as the effect on the radiation field, 3) The effect of misalignment on the radiation field is the same as that of a beam displacement, except that it is multiplied by a factor that depends on the phase advance per cell and the number of cells
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cell misalignment in accelerator structures.
the study of the effects on the dynamics of a charged particle in accelerator structures of small misalignments of the cells.

the effects of misaligned cells on the performance of accelerator structures, in particular the effects on the manifold radiation and the wakefields in the DDS1 and the uniform impedance structure, respectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cell misalignments can be modeled by beam displacements.
the effect of cell displacements is a complicated function of the displacement profile and the details of the structure.
the effects of misalignments on accelerator structures are complex and not yet completely understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell misalignment is a problem for accelerator structures.
the effect of cell alignment is equivalent to the effect of beam offset, but that the effect is not additive.

the beam displacement model works very well in the case of DDS1, and that in the case of a uniform structure, the synchronous wave aliasing effect is a general effect which is not captured by the beam displacement model, but which can be understood as the result of the interplay between wakefield and synchronous wave effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of alternating cell misalignment can be approximated as the effect of beam displacement.
the effects of cell misalignment can be very different depending on the sign of the cell misalignment and the sign of the detuning.
, in the presence of cell misalignations, the beam displacement is not a good approximation for the effect on the wakefields.
